Title: Man electrocuted in suspected cable theft at third-party electrical installation in Klang, says TNB
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 5 — An electrical accident that left a man dead at a 33kV link box along Jalan Abas in Kapar, Klang today occurred at an installation belonging to a third party and not Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), the utility company said.
Sinar Harian
reported that TNB said it was alerted to the incident at about 10am and immediately dispatched a technical team to the scene.
“The incident is believed to be linked to vandalism.
“TNB will provide its full support and cooperation to the authorities in their investigations,” it said, confirming the incident which was also shared on the TNB Careline Facebook page today.
Earlier, police confirmed that a local man in his 40s was found dead after being electrocuted, allegedly while attempting to steal electrical cables.
Klang Utara district police chief ACP Ramsay Embol said the man’s body was discovered by members of the public, who alerted the authorities.
TNB also reminded the public not to tamper with, open or approach electrical installations, warning that such actions could result in serious injury or death.

Title: Police chase Subaru from Bukit Antarabangsa to Batu Caves, two men arrested over suspected cloned car
Article:
AMPANG, Oct 5 — Police arrested two local men in their 30s after a chase involving a Subaru that began in Bukit Antarabangsa and ended in Batu Caves, Gombak, early yesterday.
Ampang Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said the operation began after the district police headquarters received information about the vehicle at about 4.36am.
He said several Mobile Patrol Vehicles (MPVs) were deployed to assist officers in pursuing the Subaru from Jalan Wangsa in Bukit Antarabangsa towards the Middle Ring Road 2 (MRR2) in Hulu Kelang.
The pursuit continued into the Batu Caves area, where police managed to stop the vehicle and arrest its two occupants, he said in a statement cited by Sinar Harian.
Khairul Anuar said preliminary checks found that the Subaru was suspected to be a cloned vehicle.
Both men also tested positive for drugs during urine screening, while police checks found that one of them was wanted in connection with a drug-related case, he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of his duties.

Title: Nine in 10 workers may feel unprepared for AI as PEOPLElogy launches National AI Readiness Week to get 5 million Malaysians ready by 2030
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Malaysia’s artificial intelligence (AI) ambitions are running up against a hard reality: the country is short of more than 500,000 AI-skilled workers, a gap large enough to threaten the RM50 billion in economic potential its AI economy is projected to unlock by 2030.
The shortfall goes beyond numbers. Various workplace studies show that, depending on the sector, as many as nine in 10 Malaysian employees feel inadequately trained to work alongside AI — leaving a significant share of that projected economic output at risk of never being realised.
In a media release, assessments by agencies such as TalentCorp have also warned that hundreds of thousands of existing roles — often cited at around 700,000 — are highly vulnerable to displacement or significant task shifts driven by AI, automation and digitalisation unless aggressive reskilling takes place.
The gap underscores a critical mismatch between traditional education pipelines and the specialised digital skills that modern industries demand.
PEOPLElogy Bhd, which describes itself as Southeast Asia’s first publicly listed digital workforce transformation company, is stepping in to help close that gap.
The company has launched National AI Readiness Week 2026 (NAIRW 2026), a five-day national platform to be held from November 12 to 18 across two venues in the Klang Valley.
NAIRW 2026 is the flagship national platform of the “I’m AI Ready” movement, a 36-month national drive launched on June 19 this year to get 5 million Malaysians to declare their AI readiness by 2030. The week is intended to bring the movement to life through large-scale public engagement, in line with the country’s broader digital economy agenda.
“We are launching National AI Readiness Week right now because the AI industry stands at a critical crossroads: while the immense economic potential of artificial intelligence is scaling rapidly, our workforce faces a widening gap between passive awareness and actual capability,” said PEOPLElogy founder and managing director Allen Lee in the media statement.
“Success for us is clear — we are driving toward 5 million public AI readiness declarations by 2030, ensuring that through verified assessments, active mastery scholarships, and unified commitments from boardrooms and businesses, the digital economy grows with no one left behind.”
Allen Lee, Founder and Managing Director of PEOPLElogy Berhad, says National AI Readiness Week 2026 aims to move Malaysians from AI awareness to real job-ready skills. — Picture courtesy of PEOPLElogy Berhad
Momentum building
The company said the movement is already gaining traction, with more than 9,100 Malaysians having declared their AI readiness as of end-September, against a target of 50,000 by the end of 2026.
More than 800 delegates have registered to attend NAIRW 2026, while the Asia AI Excellence Awards have drawn more than 200 nominations.
Three audiences, one movement
Rather than running as a single-track conference, NAIRW 2026 is deliberately structured around three distinct audiences, with the aim of moving the whole economy forward together rather than in isolated pockets.
The I’m AI READY Summit, from November 12 to 14, is aimed at SMEs, entrepreneurs, students and the wider workforce, offering practical scaling support, baseline AI-readiness assessments and personalised upskilling roadmaps.
The Build a Future Team (BAFT) Leaders Conference, on November 17 and 18, shifts the focus to corporate, human resources and government leaders, tackling organisational readiness and future-team strategy.
“The week is intentionally designed to connect the boardroom with the Rakyat simultaneously, ensuring that leadership frameworks, small business execution and individual workforce upskilling align so no one is left behind,” the organisers said.
The week will close with the Asia AI Excellence Awards, a regional gala recognising organisations that are driving measurable AI impact. Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo is scheduled to present the awards.
Excitement fills the room as hundreds of Malaysians gather for the launch of the I'm AI READY movement, many keen to find out how artificial intelligence will shape their jobs and careers. — Picture courtesy of PEOPLElogy Berhad
RM3m in AI Mastery Scholarships
Backing the movement with direct investment, PEOPLElogy is offering RM3 million in
AI Mastery Scholarships
to support Malaysians in upskilling in AI.
To draw more Malaysians into the movement, the company has also opened a nationwide
contest
offering an iPhone 18 Pro Max (512GB) as the daily prize on each day of the I’m AI READY Summit, from November 12 to 14.
Entrants must take the “Find Out Your AI Personality” quiz — the same assessment used for an official AI-readiness declaration — before registering to attend NAIRW 2026.
The movement is run in collaboration with MyDIGITAL Corporation, in line with the government’s broader digital economy agenda and efforts to strengthen the country’s pipeline of AI-ready talent.
NAIRW 2026 is the movement’s first edition, with a second edition targeted for the second quarter of 2027 as part of PEOPLElogy’s 36-month commitment to reach its goal of 5 million Malaysians.
More information and registration details are available at
imaiready.asia.

Title: BN talks with potential Melaka election partners 95pc complete, says Zahid
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 5 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has reached about 95 per cent completion in negotiations with potential partners for the Melaka election, with the coalition expected to reveal the outcome after the election date is announced on Oct 7, its chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
According to
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT) Zahid, who is also Umno president, said discussions with the parties involved were nearing completion.
“We will wait for the election date announcement on Oct 7. After that, we will announce which coalition we will work with or reach an understanding with for the Melaka election,” he told reporters after an event at Universiti Teknologi Mara here yesterday.
The parties involved appeared to refer to PAS and Pakatan Harapan (PH), according to FMT.
On Friday, PAS deputy president Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said seat negotiations with Umno were about 90 per cent complete.
Zahid said BN had yet to decide whether PAS would contest the election using the BN logo.
However, he said BN was open to PAS contesting under its own symbol.
Asked if BN was willing to negotiate with PH, Zahid said the coalition was open to discussions.

Title: Father of slain Yong Peng schoolgirl hopes justice will be served, urges public not to speculate
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Oct 5 — The father of a Form Four student who was found dead at a school in Yong Peng here hopes justice will be served for his daughter.
Mohd Khairool Faisal Khyar, 42, said the family was leaving the investigation entirely to police and the relevant authorities to ensure justice for his daughter, Irene Sofiya, 16.
“We are grateful to everyone who came and we hope justice can be served for my late daughter,” he was quoted as saying by
Sinar Harian.
He was speaking after her burial at the Kampung Arshad Muslim Cemetery in Yong Peng here yesterday.
Mohd Khairool Faisal said he only learned about the incident at about 6pm on Saturday after his eldest sister, Siti Nur Faeza Khyar, 45, contacted him and told him that Irene Sofiya, fondly known as Fiya, had been found in critical condition before being pronounced dead.
“At the time, I was working in Bangi before rushing back to the village to get more information,” he said, according to the Malay daily
He said the last time he saw Fiya was about two weeks ago and she had shown no changes in behaviour.
“In fact, Fiya looked cheerful and was happy to be studying,” he said.
Mohd Khairool Faisal also urged the public not to spread inaccurate speculation about the incident involving his daughter,
Sinar Harian
reported.

Title: Don’t skimp on third-party insurance, and think twice about Waze, Consul General tells Malaysians driving to Thailand
Article:
SONGKHLA, Oct 5 — Malaysians driving their own vehicles into Thailand are advised to obtain insurance coverage that includes third-party claims in the event of a road accident in the country.
Consul General of Malaysia in Songkhla Ahmad Fahmi Ahmad Sarkawi said such insurance is crucial if a Malaysian driver is found to have caused an accident resulting in injury or death, potentially requiring substantial compensation.
“Usually, apart from the penalty imposed on the offender, there is also an element where Malaysians need to pay compensation to the injured (victim) or the deceased’s family as a result of the accident.
“The compensation or damages involved are not small amounts. Therefore, adequate insurance can also cover the compensation costs,” he said during a courtesy call by a delegation from the Perlis Journalists Association at the Consulate General of Malaysia in Songkhla here last Friday (Oct 2).
Ahmad Fahmi said his office had encountered cases of Malaysian drivers involved in accidents in Thailand who did not have sufficient funds to pay compensation to victims, as they only had insurance coverage for hospital medical costs.
He also advised Malaysians visiting the country to obtain insurance coverage for vehicle damage caused by natural disasters.
Meanwhile, Ahmad Fahmi said Malaysians were not encouraged to travel at night, especially in high-risk areas such as Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat, following security incidents in the three southern Thai provinces.
He also recommended that they use only Apple Maps or Google Maps when travelling to destinations in southern Thailand, as these were safer options than Waze, which might direct road users through shortcuts into villages and hilly areas. — Bernama

Title: Irene Sofiya, 16, laid to rest in Batu Pahat cemetery after school hall death in Yong Peng
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Oct 5 — Sixteen-year-old Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, who was killed in an incident at a school in Yong Peng, was laid to rest at the Kampung Parit Arshad Muslim Cemetery here at about 7.50pm yesterday.
Earlier, her remains were brought to her grandmother’s home in Kampung Parit Selamat, Yong Peng, at about 6.30pm following a post-mortem at Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital here.
More than 100 family members, relatives, school friends, teachers and locals were at the cemetery to pay their final respects.
The teenager was found unconscious and covered in blood in a school hall in Yong Peng at about 5.50pm yesterday.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the victim suffered multiple injuries to the head and body and was pronounced dead at the scene.
A 16-year-old boy was detained in the Yong Peng area at about 7pm the same day and remanded for six days until Oct 9 to assist investigations.
Police are investigating the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code, while the motive and circumstances remain under investigation. — Bernama

Title: Four dead, child seriously injured after Axia crashes into lorry on Gerik-Jeli highway
Article:
IPOH, Oct 5 — The fatal crash in Gerik, which claimed the lives of four people, including a child, was believed to have occurred after the Perodua Axia they were travelling in lost control before crashing into a lorry at KM 38.5 of the East-West Highway (JRTB) Gerik-Jeli, near Tasik Banding.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said police received information about the accident involving three vehicles – a Hino lorry, a Proton Persona and a Perodua Axia – at about 1.30pm yesterday.
He said preliminary investigations found that the Perodua Axia, driven by a 19-year-old man with four passengers – a 31-year-old man, a 40-year-old woman and two children – was travelling from Gerik towards Jeli.
At the same time, the Proton Persona, driven by a 20-year-old man with three passengers, was travelling in the opposite direction from Jeli, Kelantan towards Gerik, while a lorry driven by a 42-year-old man with a 34-year-old male attendant was also travelling in the same direction.
“Based on preliminary investigations, the Perodua Axia is believed to have lost control before entering the opposite lane and hitting the rear side of the Proton Persona before crashing into the front of the lorry behind the Proton Persona.
“The impact caused the Perodua Axia to become wedged underneath the lorry and be dragged for about three to seven metres,” he said in a statement last night.
Mohd Alwi said four victims in the Perodua Axia, comprising two men, a woman and a child, were pronounced dead, while another child was seriously injured and taken to Gerik Hospital for treatment.
He said the driver and passengers of the Proton Persona, as well as the lorry driver and attendant, were not injured.
“An inspection of the scene has been conducted, and photographs were taken to assist investigations. All three vehicles involved will be sent for technical inspection.
“Efforts to identify independent witnesses and obtain closed-circuit television (CCTV) and dashcam footage, if available, are also underway,” he said, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Members of the public with information about the accident are urged to come forward to assist investigations. — Bernama

Title: DKU rejects claim Tuanku Muhriz has ceased to be Negeri Sembilan ruler
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 5 — The Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) has once again reaffirmed that Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir remains the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
DKU secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin said Tuanku Muhriz was elected by the Undangs and proclaimed as the 11th Yang Dipertuan Besar on Dec 29, 2008, before being officially installed in accordance with the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 (UUTKNS) on Oct 26, 2009.
He said Tuanku Muhriz continued to hold the position, as well as serving as chairman of the DKU under Article 19.
“The UUTKNS 1959 provides that the only lawful way for the position to become vacant is if it is established that the Undangs have called upon His Royal Highness to abdicate or step down. Article 10 requires a proper and full enquiry by the Undangs; a determination that the grounds specified under Article 10 exist.
“The exercise of that power by persons lawfully holding the office of Undang in the number required under Article 29; and a proclamation under Article 10(2),” he said in a statement yesterday.
Raja Norazli said none of these requirements had been fulfilled.
He said Tuanku Muhriz had continued to discharge the functions of the Yang Dipertuan Besar since April 19, while the council continued to sit with His Royal Highness as its chairman.
As such, he said there was no vacancy in the office of Yang Dipertuan Besar.
“Article 11 only applies when the position is vacant, and could not be invoked to elect a successor as long as the office is lawfully occupied.
“The tenure of Tuanku Muhriz in the position can only be terminated in the manner provided for under the UUTKNS 1959. The council does not recognise any other person as holding the position,” he said.
Raja Norazli Raja Nordin, secretary of the Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU), reads his special statement at his office in Seremban, October 4, 2026. — Bernama pic
Meanwhile, Raja Norazli said Tuanku Muhriz did not intervene in Luak Sungei Ujong affairs during the April 17 sitting.
He said the records showed that the matter brought before the DKU was a complaint lodged by representatives of the Telaga Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong, namely Ibu Soko and Waris Klana Hulu.
“They dismissed Mubarak Thahak @ Dohak as Undang in accordance with the customs of the Luak, with the dismissal letter handed to him on May 13, 2025.
“He said Tuanku Muhriz had made it clear that, under Article 14(1) and (3), the customary authority to choose, appoint and dismiss an Undang rests with the Luak itself, and that no member of the Dewan, ‘including His Royal Highness himself’, has the power to support or oppose such a decision,” he said.
He said the DKU therefore recognised the dismissal as a decision by the Luak under its own customs under Article 14(3).
“The members were consulted before the conclusion was reached, and the minutes showed that no further objections were raised after Tuanku Muhriz, as Speaker of the Dewan, announced the Dewan’s decision to accept the dismissal,” he said.
He said neither the DKU nor Tuanku Muhriz had dismissed any Undang.
Raja Norazli explained that the Dewan accepted the Luak’s decision to dismiss the Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong.
“Therefore, the April 17 sitting was not an intervention in the affairs of the Luak. Rather, it was the Dewan carrying out its function under Article 16 to receive and advise on a decision already made by the Luak in accordance with its customs,” he said.
Raja Norazli also said the Luak had dismissed Mubarak Thahak @ Dohak as Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong under its customs, effective May 13, 2025 (advice dated April 17, 2026).
Maarof Mat Rashad, meanwhile, was dismissed as Undang of Luak Jelebu under the Luak’s customs, effective May 31, 2023 (advice dated July 31, 2026).
“Abdul Rahim Yasin was never formally appointed as Undang of Luak Rembau in accordance with the prescribed customs because his appointment was never completed through the Istiadat Menzahirkan Kejadian Undang ceremony (advice dated July 31),” he said.
Raja Norazli said Badarudin Abdul Khalid had ceased to hold the position of Dato’ Shahbandar Sungei Ujong following a Luruh Pusaka declaration by anak waris and Ibu Soko Waris di Ayer on July 30, 2026, which was affirmed on July 31, 2026.
“Therefore, the current Undang are Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari for Luak Sungei Ujong and Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid for Luak Rembau.
“Datuk Johan Pahlawan Lela Perkasa Setiawan Datuk Muhammed Abdullah is the Undang of Luak Johol, while the positions of Undang of Luak Jelebu and Dato’ Shahbandar Sungei Ujong are currently vacant,” he said.
He said the DKU had therefore maintained its decision of July 31, 2026 that the document dated April 19, 2026 did not comply with Article 10, was unconstitutional and had no effect, and that no valid process had resulted in Tuanku Muhriz ceasing to hold the position of Yang Dipertuan Besar.
Raja Norazli also said the DKU continued to recognise Tuanku Muhriz as Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan and Speaker of the Dewan under Article 19, did not recognise any vacancy in either position, and did not recognise anyone else as holding them.
He said the DKU also called on all state and federal civil servants to continue administering the state in accordance with the law and the lawful chain of command, and required anyone claiming that a “sufficient and full investigation” had been conducted to present the complete record of the process before a forum with jurisdiction.
“All parties are also urged to respect court proceedings, maintain public order, and not invoke custom as a reason to disregard the UUTKNS 1959,” he said. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: The initials UUTKNS stands for Undang-Undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan, the Malay term for the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan.

Title: Sultan Ibrahim’s close Bahrain ties helped bring F1 back to Sepang, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The close ties between His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa paved the way for Malaysia to host the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP), said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said Malaysia’s selection as host reflected the international community’s confidence in the country and further strengthened its standing as a respected and trusted partner on the global stage.
“I pay tribute to His Majesty the King for the leadership and wisdom, and for His Majesty’s close relationship with Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, which paved the way for Malaysia to be selected as host of the 2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix,” he said in a post on X yesterday.
Anwar said he also hoped the cooperation would further reinforce ties between Malaysia and Bahrain and create opportunities for broader cooperation that would benefit the people of both countries.
The Prime Minister said he joined His Majesty and Bahrain Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa to watch the race at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).
“I also had the opportunity to meet and speak with royal guests who attended today’s race, including the Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah Mu’izzaddin Waddaulah ibni Al-Marhum Sultan Haji Omar ‘Ali Saifuddien Sa’adul Khairi Waddien, as well as other distinguished guests,” he said.
The F1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP 2026, held from October 2 to 4, marked F1’s return to Sepang after a nine-year absence, with the circuit last hosting a race in 2017. — Bernama

Title: Anwar praises drivers, teams for ‘incredible action’ at Sepang F1 race
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit as a deeply meaningful memory for sports fans from around the world.
In a Facebook post yesterday, Anwar said the magnificent action delivered by all the drivers and teams also made the race full of excitement and intense competition.
“Thank you to all the drivers and teams for the incredible action presented to fans from around the world, making the race in Sepang this time a truly meaningful memory,” he said in the post.
Anwar, along with the Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Bahrain, Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, also presented trophies to the drivers and teams that triumphed in the race.
He also congratulated Max Verstappen, Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton, as well as the Red Bull Racing team, on their achievements.
Last July, F1 confirmed Malaysia as the host of the 2026 Gulf Air Bahrain GP from October 2 to 4 following an agreement between Formula 1, the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
Although the circuit was drenched by rain, the excitement in the grandstands did not wane in the slightest, reflecting how deeply fans missed F1 after nine years of the sport’s absence from Malaysia. — Bernama

Title: Suhakam doesn’t need prosecutorial powers — but govt must answer its findings, says chairman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) does not need prosecutorial powers to be effective, but authorities should be required to respond to its findings and recommendations, its chairman Datuk Seri Mohd Hishamudin Md Yunus said.
While the 77-year-old former judge acknowledged criticism of Suhakam’s limitations, he stressed that the national human rights body was far from being a “toothless” organisation.
Instead, he urged critics to recognise that Suhakam has a distinct role from the courts, enforcement agencies and other statutory bodies.
“Suhakam’s present mandate is primarily investigative, advisory, educational and recommendatory.
“We are not a court, and we do not have prosecutorial powers,” Mohd Hishamudin told
Malay Mail
in an exclusive interview recently.
“Suhakam already has important investigative powers under Act 597 (the Suhakam Act). We can initiate inquiries, summon witnesses, obtain evidence and make recommendations.
“The 2024 amendments also strengthened our mandate to visit places of detention, institutions and other relevant places,” he added, referring to the latest amendments to the Suhakam Act, which took effect in July 2024.
Mohd Hishamudin said the broader powers enabled the commission to conduct a thorough and independent public inquiry into the Taiping prison riot that occurred in January 2025.
The riot, involving about 100 inmates, resulted in the death of a High Court detainee.
Suhakam’s inquiry later found that a large number of prison officers had used excessive physical violence against the detainees and abused weapons and security equipment, including batons and pepper spray.
It also flagged serious overcrowding at Taiping Prison and recommended that the 146-year-old building be turned into a museum as it was no longer fit to serve as a prison.
A prison officer had already been charged under Section 304(b) of the Penal Code in December 2025, while another five Taiping Prison wardens were charged in July 2026 over injuries allegedly inflicted on inmates.
The real gap comes after investigations
At present, Suhakam can publish findings from a public inquiry and make recommendations to the relevant authorities.
While the amended law requires relevant authorities to inform Suhakam of any action taken after a human rights infringement is referred to them, it does not oblige them to accept or implement the commission’s recommendations.
The facade of Taiping Prison is seen in this undated photograph. — Picture via Penjara Taiping
Mohd Hishamudin said a stronger “respond and explain” mechanism was needed from the government to close that gap and strengthen reforms.
“Suhakam is not proposing that every recommendation automatically becomes legally binding,” he said.
Instead, he said authorities should be required to provide a written response within a reasonable period stating whether they accept, partially accept or reject a recommendation made by Suhakam.
For accepted recommendations, authorities should also provide a progress report setting out follow-up measures and a timeline for implementation, while rejected recommendations should be accompanied by reasons, he added.
Mohd Hishamudin said Malaysia could consider emulating Australia, where Section 46 of the Australian Human Rights Commission Act 1986 requires specified commission reports to be tabled in each House of Parliament within 15 sitting days of being received by the minister.
Still an ‘A-status’ rights body
Suhakam was also re-accredited as an “A-status” national human rights institution last June — recognition that Mohd Hishamudin said reflected its standing as an independent, credible and effective institution internationally.
Suhakam undergoes re-accreditation every five years by the Global Alliance of National Human Rights Institutions (GANHRI) Sub-Committee on Accreditation (SCA).
The “A-status” allows Suhakam to participate fully in international and regional human rights mechanisms, including the United Nations Human Rights Council and treaty body processes.
Nevertheless, Mohd Hishamudin stressed that credibility begins at home.
“Malaysians must have confidence that when they approach Suhakam, raise concerns or lodge complaints, they are engaging with an institution that is independent, impartial and able to carry out its mandate without undue interference,” he said.
Established through an Act of Parliament on September 9, 1999, Suhakam marked its 27th anniversary this year.
“After 27 years, the question is no longer simply whether Suhakam can investigate and make recommendations.
“The next stage of institutional reform should ensure that those recommendations receive a timely, reasoned and transparent response from the authorities concerned,” Mohd Hishamudin said.

Title: Sabah gives more than 500 adults second chance to learn reading, writing, counting
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 4 — More than 500 adults in Sabah who missed out on formal education are being given a second chance to master basic reading, writing and counting (3M) skills through the Functional Literacy Education Programme (PLF) organised by the Community Development Department (KEMAS).
Sabah KEMAS director Ahmad Fakhrul Azman Muhammad Radzi said the participants are attending 25 classes this year in urban fringe, rural and remote areas across Kudat, Kota Marudu, Kota Belud, Keningau, Tenom, Nabawan, Beluran, Sandakan, Kinabatangan, Lahad Datu, Semporna, Tawau and Kalabakan.
The programme primarily targets individuals aged between 15 and 65 who have yet to master basic 3M skills, while those outside the age range can also participate based on their needs.
“PLF is among the efforts to eradicate illiteracy, particularly among those who dropped out of formal education at an early stage and are still unable to read, write and count,” he told Bernama.
Participants are identified with the help of community leaders, including village heads, as well as KEMAS teachers on the ground, who provide information on individuals still in need of literacy education.
Before joining the classes, participants sit for a pre-test to assess their initial reading, writing and counting skills. A post-test is conducted upon completion to measure their progress, with more than 70 per cent recorded as achieving an excellent level.
Those who have yet to fully master the three skills can repeat the lessons to ensure they reach the required level.
Ahmad Fakhrul said regular PLF classes run for a year and are conducted by KEMAS-appointed PLF community development officers who serve as trained educators in the targeted areas.
Classes conducted by additional instructors in areas with greater needs run for six months, with three sessions a week.
As part of efforts to recognise participants and encourage them to continue learning, graduation ceremonies are held according to class and district.
A total of 375 participants from 25 classes took part in this year’s ceremonies, which were conducted by groups and according to their respective districts.
“Participants who complete the programme receive certificates as recognition and encouragement to continue learning. We do not know whether they may eventually become interested in pursuing further education,” he said.
Beyond literacy, KEMAS instructors also expose participants to livelihood and entrepreneurship skills through the production of items such as handicrafts, fish crackers and rempeyek, based on local needs.
“We want participants to apply their basic 3M skills in small-scale entrepreneurship so that they can indirectly generate income,” said Ahmad Fakhrul.
As technology advances, PLF participants are also introduced to digital skills to help them keep pace with current developments and reduce the digital divide.
They are guided in using smartphones for everyday tasks, including making clinic appointments through the MySejahtera application and paying bills, as well as promoting their products online
“Efforts to eradicate illiteracy must continue and receive support from all parties so that no one, particularly in Sabah, is left behind in education.
“We do not want them to be easily deceived in their daily affairs because of literacy limitations. Instead, they should be supported until they can become independent and live their lives with greater confidence,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: F1 excitement at Sepang also brings opportunities for local traders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The return of Formula 1 (F1) to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after a nine-year absence has not only delighted motorsport fans but also provided an opportunity for about 40 local traders to earn an income through the Karnival Litar Rasa Madani.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the carnival, held at the G Hillstand at SIC in conjunction with the 2026 F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP), brought together local traders offering a variety of food and beverages, including snacks and light refreshments.
He said that the lively atmosphere at the circuit also gave visitors an opportunity to enjoy local fare while watching the race and, at the same time, supporting local traders.
“I took the opportunity to visit the G Hillstand at the Sepang International Circuit, which accommodates most of the Madani ticket holders, while meeting F1 fans.
“The atmosphere here is lively, with an interesting view of the circuit as well as the Karnival Litar Rasa Madani While enjoying the race at the circuit, visitors can also enjoy a meal and support our traders!” Anwar said in a Facebook post today.
The Prime Minister added that the organisation of the Karnival Litar Rasa Madani was one of the efforts to ensure that the excitement surrounding F1 also generated economic benefits for local traders.
“My appreciation to the Ministry of Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives (KUSKOP), the Ministry of Youth and Sports (KBS) and all agencies involved in making this carnival a success, thereby ensuring that the excitement surrounding F1 also brings greater opportunities for local traders,” he said.
In July, F1 confirmed Malaysia as the host of the Gulf Air Bahrain GP, from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement between Formula 1, the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The return of F1 to Malaysia followed discussions and cooperation involving His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and King of Bahrain, King Hamad bin Isa Al-Khalifa; as well as the two governments, to retain the Bahrain GP on the 2026 F1 calendar, after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia previously hosted the Malaysian GP at SIC from 1999 to 2017, before being dropped from the F1 calendar. — Bernama

Title: Zahid urges UiTM to establish Quantum Department, says Malaysia must not lag
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 4 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has called on Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) to establish a Quantum Department to ensure the country does not lag behind current advancements.
He said the department is targeted to be established next year to ensure local expertise can be developed at an early stage.
“AI is indeed good and is being implemented very well, but quantum is a new technology based on the latest technological developments, and Malaysia should not lag behind in this area.
“I am very confident that its potential is immense in attracting many students to pursue studies in this field and eventually, in less than a decade, producing quantum experts in our country,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also the Rural and Regional Development Minister, said this after officiating the ‘Wacana Semarak Patriotisme: Seminar Ilmuwan Islam’ at the university’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor here today.
Quantum technology is an advanced field of science and engineering that harnesses properties of quantum mechanics, such as superposition and entanglement of subatomic particles, to process information at extraordinary speeds.
Ahmad Zahid said his ministry would also contribute RM500,000 to UiTM to support the development of programmes such as the TVET UiTM Dihatiku training and certification programme and UTAMA PLUS UiTM AI Certified, including the development of the Quantum Department. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia eyes F1 calendar return as PM Anwar confirms talks under way
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Malaysia is discussing a possible return to the Formula One calendar beyond this weekend’s race at Sepang, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today, raising hopes of a longer-term revival of the Malaysian Grand Prix.
Anwar confirmed the talks during a brief exchange with Sky Sports commentator Martin Brundle on the grid at the Sepang International Circuit ahead of today’s Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
Asked by Brundle about the prospect of Malaysia returning to the F1 calendar in future, Anwar replied: “Well, I’m looking forward to it. We are discussing.”
The remark is the clearest indication yet that Putrajaya is considering extending Malaysia’s renewed association with Formula One beyond this weekend, which marked the sport’s first race at Sepang in nine years.
Drenched after heavy rain swept across the circuit and delayed the start, Anwar nevertheless said the mood surrounding Formula One’s return had been overwhelmingly positive.
“Oh yes. You see, I’m wet, drenched, but excited. You see, the entire country is rejoicing,” he told Brundle.
Formula One returned to Sepang this weekend for the first time since 2017 after the Bahrain Grand Prix was relocated to Malaysia because of security concerns linked to conflict in the Middle East.
The October 2-4 race retained its official Bahrain Grand Prix designation and was arranged as a one-off event.
Malaysia previously hosted a Formula One race annually from 1999 until 2017, when the government ended the event amid concerns over high costs and diminishing returns.
The economics of a permanent comeback remain a major hurdle.
Sepang International Circuit chief executive Azhan Shafriman Hanif has said Malaysia would require at least RM300 million a year to secure a regular place on the F1 calendar, with any return also dependent on a slot becoming available.
By contrast, Malaysia’s expenditure for this weekend’s event was estimated at between RM10 million and RM16 million because Bahrain had already borne the major hosting costs.

Title: Brunei Sultan departs after witnessing F1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP return to Sepang
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 4 — The Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, departed for home today after concluding his special visit in conjunction with the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).
The aircraft carrying His Majesty and the Brunei delegation, including Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, took off at 5.30 pm after a red carpet send-off, which included a guard of honour mounted by 28 officers and personnel from the First Battalion of the Royal Malay Regiment.
Minister of Youth and Sports Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari, Brunei High Commissioner to Malaysia Dato Paduka Abdu’r Rahmani Basir and Chief of Protocol Ambassador Mohd Ikram Ibrahim were present at the Bunga Raya Complex here to bid farewell to His Majesty and his delegation.
Earlier, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah attended the F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at SIC with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and the top leaders of Malaysia, Bahrain and Brunei to witness the return of the prestigious F1 race to Sepang after a nine-year absence.
Also attending the race were Bahrain Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
In July, F1 confirmed Malaysia as the host venue for the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement between Formula 1, the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
F1’s return to Malaysia followed discussions and cooperation involving His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim and Bahrain’s King Hamad Isa Al-Khalifa, as well as the two governments, to retain the Bahrain Grand Prix on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia previously hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix at SIC from 1999 to 2017 before being dropped from the F1 calendar. — Bernama

Title: Boy mauled by pack of five stray dogs in Bachok receives rabies jab, shows signs of recovery
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 4 — An eight-year-old boy who was seriously injured after being attacked by a pack of stray dogs at Pantai Kuala Kemasin, Bachok, on Thursday has received a rabies vaccination and is now being monitored for three weeks.
The boy’s mother, Rosnani Mat Salleh, 46, said her son, Azuar Firdaus Zuraiman, showed positive progress today after remaining withdrawn for two days as he was still traumatised by the incident.
“For two days after the incident, he was still frightened and did not want to talk. He mostly kept to himself and sometimes cried because he was in pain from his injuries, especially to his head and neck.
“Thankfully, his condition has improved today and he has started talking. He can now answer when asked and can recount what happened during the incident,” she told reporters at Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital here today.
Earlier, Rosnani and her son were visited by the Kelantan Education Department (JPN) Student Development Sector deputy director, Norazan Mat Nor.
Recalling the incident, Rosnani said Azuar Firdaus was playing on the beach around 9.30 am with three relatives when five stray dogs approached.
She said the three relatives, aged between two and 11, managed to run away, but Azuar Firdaus fell while trying to escape and became the dogs’ target.
“He tried to escape by running into the sea, but the dogs continued chasing him until someone came to his aid and rescued him. He was semi-conscious after the incident and suffered injuries to his head, neck and hand, including bite wounds, in addition to scratches on his back,” she said.
Rosnani said her son underwent a five-hour surgery the day after the incident to treat his injuries.
She said Azuar Firdaus also received a rabies vaccination and is expected to continue being monitored for about three weeks.
Meanwhile, Norazan said the department is aware of the incident, which is believed to be the first involving a student being seriously injured in a stray dog attack.
He added that the victim has shown positive progress and is expected to be discharged from hospital today. — Bernama

Title: Amanah says Pakatan open to partners to form stable Melaka govt ahead of state election
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 4  — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to seeking allies to form a stable government in Melaka in the upcoming state election, said Amanah secretary-general Muhammad Faiz Fadzil.
He said Amanah’s stand was that it was better for the coalition to find partners who could work together to form a stable state government.
Muhammad Faiz said a decision on possible cooperation was expected to be made soon but the possibility of PH contesting on its own remained open.
“Amanah believes that joining forces with allies who want to establish a stable government in Melaka would be better,” he told reporters after the LKIM chairman’s engagement session with Telok Mas fishermen at the Tanjong Nibong fishermen’s jetty here today.
Muhammad Faiz said any decision on political cooperation would be determined by the PH Presidential Council, but Amanah had been exploring collaboration with various parties.
In the 2021 state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 seats contested, while PH took five and Perikatan Nasional two.
The Election Commission is meeting on Wednesday to set the dates for the state polls. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan joins Johor on unhealthy air list as haze lingers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — A total of eight locations recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the unhealthy category as of 4pm today.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, five areas in Johor were affected, involving Segamat (156), Batu Pahat (155), Kluang (152), Tangkak (151) and Larkin (111).
In Negeri Sembilan, the affected areas were Nilai (151) and Seremban (146), while Samarahan, Sarawak, recorded a reading of 117.
Meanwhile, 57 areas were in the moderate category, while three areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and an API exceeding 300 hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Another woman files report against motivational speaker as Perlis police probe alleged sexual harassment
Article:
KANGAR, Oct 4 — Perlis police have confirmed receiving another report against a male motivational speaker over an allegation of sexual harassment.
Perlis police chief DCP Hamzah Hashim said the report was received yesterday and involved a 19-year-old female complainant.
“The case is being investigated under Section 509 of the Penal Code, Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act,” he said in a statement today.
Hamzah said the man is currently under a two-day remand order ending today in connection with a police report lodged in Padang Besar.
He said the motivational speaker would be released on police bail before being re-arrested by Kangar police for further action.
He added that an application for remand to assist investigations into the Kangar case would be made at the Kangar Magistrates’ Court tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: F1 roars back at Sepang as Sultan Ibrahim, Bahrain and Brunei royals watch on
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 4 — The return of Formula 1 to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after a nine-year absence received special attention today when His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, attended the 2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix F1 race, together with the top leaders of Malaysia, Bahrain and Brunei.
His Majesty was received on arrival at about 2.15 pm by Bahrain Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Also attending the race were the Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, and Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, who were received by Anwar at about 2.35 pm.
The Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah; the Tunku Mahkota of Kedah, Tunku Shazuddin Ariff Sultan Sallehuddin; and the Tengku Mahkota of Kelantan, Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra; also attended the race, marking the return of the roar of F1 engines to Sepang after the last race was held there in 2017.
The race, scheduled to start at 3 pm, was slightly delayed due to heavy rain after Negaraku and the Bahrain national anthem were played.
The event is expected to attract nearly 100,000 spectators and will also feature a fly-past by Gulf Air aircraft before the race gets underway.
Cars enter the pit lane after the start of theGulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix F1 race was delayed by heavy rain at the Sepang International Circuit on October 4, 2026, which marks F1’s return to Malaysia after a nine-year absence. — AFP pic
Four-time world champion Max Verstappen of Red Bull Racing will start the 56-lap race from pole position, followed by seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari and current championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes-AMG Petronas.
In July, F1 confirmed Malaysia as the host venue for the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement between Formula 1, the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), and the Malaysian and Bahraini governments.
F1’s return to Malaysia followed discussions and cooperation involving His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim and Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al-Khalifa, as well as the two governments, to retain the Bahrain Grand Prix on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia previously hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix at SIC from 1999 to 2017 before the race was dropped from the F1 calendar. — Bernama

Title: Motorcycle skids towards drain near Taiping, killing 76-year-old rider
Article:
IPOH, Oct 4 — An elderly man was killed and a woman who was the pillion rider was seriously injured after the motorcycle they were riding skidded at Lorong Kampung Boyan 1, Kampung Boyan near Taiping, today.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department Assistant Director of Operations Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the 76-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene by Ministry of Health (MOH) medical officers.
He said they received a call about the incident at 12.41 pm before a fire engine from the Taiping Fire and Rescue Station arrived six minutes later.
“Upon arriving at the scene, personnel found that the Yamaha Ego motorcycle ridden by the two victims had skidded and nearly fallen into a drain in front of a house. The elderly man was unconscious while the 69-year-old woman suffered serious head injuries,” he said in a statement today.
Sabarodzi said firefighters lifted the male victim, who was nearly falling into the drain, before MOH medical officers confirmed his death.
“The injured victim was given initial treatment before being sent to the hospital, while the male victim’s body was handed over to the police for further action, and the operation ended at 1.49 pm,” he said. — Bernama

Title: After F1 and KL Marathon, October’s only getting busier with Melaka election dates on Wednesday and Budget Friday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — October has got off to a positive start for Malaysia, marked by a vibrant sporting calendar, strong performances by national athletes and encouraging developments in the economy and investment, while several major national agendas await as the month unfolds.
The first weekend of the month saw Malaysia become a focal point for sports fans as the roar of Formula 1 (F1) machinery once again echoed at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after nine years, with Malaysia hosting the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026.
The return of the prestigious race to Sepang, which last hosted an F1 event in 2017, coincided with two other major international sporting events, the Le Tour de Langkawi (LTdL) 2026 and the Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon (KLSCM) 2026.
The 30th edition of LTdL, which began on Sept 27, will conclude in Putrajaya today after eight stages across the peninsula, while KLSCM, held yesterday and today, saw more than 30,000 local and international participants take to the streets of the capital.
The sporting excitement at home was accompanied by strong performances by the national contingent at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games in Japan, which had secured nine gold, seven silver and 16 bronze medals as of yesterday.
The haul included historic team gold medals for the men’s and women’s squash teams, a keirin gold for track cycling champion Datuk Mohd Azizulhasni Awang, and the men’s sepak takraw squad’s first team regu gold in 36 years.
National sporting success also extended to the football pitch as Harimau Malaya ended their Fifa Asean Cup 2026 group-stage campaign with a 6-0 victory over Singapore.
Although the result was not enough to send the national squad into the final, the team is set to face Vietnam in the third-place playoff tomorrow.
The positive trend was also reflected in the economy, with the ringgit showing resilience in a challenging global environment, ending the first week of October trading at 4.0820/4.0870 against the US dollar.
Malaysia’s investment momentum also received a boost as the country and Singapore explored efforts to attract third-country investors to the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).
Companies from the republic have so far committed more than S$5.5 billion in investments in the zone, covering sectors including advanced manufacturing, data centres, energy technology and solar energy.
On the international front, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia’s involvement was also expanding through Petronas, which holds a 25 per cent stake in the C$33 billion (about RM94.7 billion) LNG Canada Phase 2 expansion project.
The project could open up further investment and business opportunities for Malaysian companies in Canada’s energy and infrastructure sectors.
Following Anwar’s meeting with Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister, Prince Salman Hamad Al Khalifa, yesterday, Malaysia also welcomed Bahraini investments in areas including Islamic finance, technology, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and smart manufacturing.
The two countries also encouraged Malaysian companies to use Bahrain as a gateway to the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) market.
Despite the positive developments at the start of October, Malaysia continues to grapple with transboundary haze, which has caused a decline in air quality in many areas nationwide.
Six areas recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels, while 37 were at moderate levels and only three recorded good readings.
As October progresses, attention will turn to several major agendas expected to shape the country’s economic and political landscape for the remainder of the year.
Most immediately, focus will be on the Dewan Rakyat sitting, which begins tomorrow, with the tabling of Budget 2027 by the Prime Minister, who is also Finance Minister, scheduled for Friday.
The budget will be among the country’s most closely watched economic agendas this year, with attention expected on measures to tackle the cost of living, raise incomes, stimulate growth and strengthen economic resilience amid a challenging global environment.
The Pre-Budget 2027 Statement had outlined 10 focus areas centred on the Madani Economy and 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) priorities, including tackling the cost of living, increasing incomes, creating quality jobs and strengthening the economy and governance.
Political activity is also expected to intensify this month as the 16th Melaka State Election (PRN) moves into the next phase following the dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly on Sept 23.
The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting this Wednesday to determine key dates for the election, including nomination and polling days, as negotiations and cooperation among political parties remain a focal point.
Senior Lecturer in Political Science at the Faculty of Administrative Science and Policy Studies, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), Mujibu Abd Muis, described October as a crucial month that could determine the direction and pace of the country’s politics in the final months of 2026.
He said developments taking place almost simultaneously, including the Melaka state election, internal party dynamics and the tabling of Budget 2027, could shape public perceptions ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16).
Mujibu viewed the Melaka state election not merely as a battleground to determine the state government, but as a potential ‘political laboratory’ for parties to test their respective strengths, strategies and cooperation formulas.
He said the election would follow two previous state polls involving Johor and Negeri Sembilan, while also providing political data that could influence seat negotiations, candidate selection and coalition alignments ahead of GE16.
Mujibu said Budget 2027 would serve as the most tangible test of the government’s economic credibility, noting that the public would evaluate it not merely based on figures but on the extent to which announced measures affect their lives, including disposable income, the cost of living, employment and economic opportunities.
“With two months remaining until the end of 2026, October provides an opportunity to assess the political landscape. Parties will look at the Melaka state election results, gauge the public’s response to the Budget, assess their respective organisational strengths and then begin making more serious calculations for GE16.
“In summary, October may not be the month that determines who will win the general election, but it could be the month that determines who starts to emerge as being in the lead, who is losing momentum and who needs to change their strategy,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Petros assurance rings hollow amid challenge to Petronas, says Zaid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Former law minister Datuk Zaid Ibrahim says Sarawak premier Abang Johari Openg’s assurance that Petros will not undermine Petronas rings hollow while the state oil company seeks a bigger role in the gas business and Sarawak continues to question the federal legal framework governing petroleum.
Writing on Facebook, Zaid said the central issue was Petros’s desire to take over the gas aggregator role currently performed by Petronas in Sarawak.
That role is integral to the gas value chain, he said, and cannot be transferred without affecting Petronas’s commercial position. He estimated Petronas’s Sarawak gas business at about RM10 billion annually.
Zaid said the impact was already visible in the confusion created by competing claims over payments. He pointed to the Shell dispute, saying roughly RM80 million a month had been withheld while the parties disputed who should be paid.
Abang Johari had said earlier that Petros’s expansion was not designed to displace Petronas. He said Sarawak would continue to work with Petronas while developing its ability to process gas locally and move into higher-value downstream activities.
His comments followed Petros’s joint development agreement with Norwegian company Höegh Evi for a Kuching LNG regasification terminal, which is expected to be operational by 2029. Sarawak is also exploring small-scale LNG facilities and carbon capture, utilisation and storage projects.
Zaid said those ambitions need not be incompatible with Sarawak’s development, but the order of discussion mattered. The state must first recognise Petronas’s rights over Malaysia’s oil and gas under the Petroleum Development Act 1974, he said.
He noted that Sarawak was challenging the application of the PDA and other federal petroleum laws in the state. That, he said, was a challenge to the legal foundation of Petronas, rather than a routine negotiation over commercial participation.
Once the legal position is accepted, Zaid said, the parties can negotiate a role for Petros that addresses Sarawak’s circumstances without dismantling key functions of the national oil company.
He warned that the consequences would extend beyond Sarawak if other producing states pursued similar claims. Petronas would lose the scale that supports its national role, including its ability to invest and contribute to federal revenue, he said.

Title: JPJ hunts illegal motorcycle ride operators ferrying passengers to Sepang F1 circuit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) is tracking down individuals and groups offering illegal motorcycle ride-hailing services to transport visitors and spectators attending the Formula One (F1) Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).
According to
Berita Harian
, the operators were found advertising their services through various social media platforms, offering rides from several locations to the circuit grounds and between SIC and nearby parking areas.
A survey of social media postings showed that both car and motorcycle transport services were being promoted, although motorcycles appeared to be the preferred option among spectators seeking to avoid heavy traffic congestion around the circuit.
On Threads, some riders were offering trips between Mitsui Outlet Park Sepang and SIC for RM10 each way. Others advertised motorcycle taxi services, commonly referred to as “gojek”, charging RM10 for journeys between Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 (KLIA2) and SIC.
The report also found touts offering rides for as much as RM80 for a 10-kilometre journey from Mitsui Outlet Park to a Petronas station near the main entrance of the circuit. Some operators were also said to provide helmets for passengers.
While the services have attracted visitors looking for a faster alternative to traffic-clogged roads, concerns have been raised over safety risks, particularly in the event of accidents or other unforeseen incidents.
JPJ is understood to be conducting an enforcement operation around SIC and several hotspot locations near the circuit and KLIA. Authorities are also taking action based on information and advertisements that have gone viral on social media.
The enforcement comes amid an influx of spectators attending the F1 Bahrain Grand Prix, with traffic congestion around the Sepang circuit area drawing widespread attention over the weekend.

Title: Government to follow legal process over Bandar Utama school stabbing suit, says deputy law minister
Article:
IPOH, Oct 4 — The government will allow due process to take its course following a civil suit filed by the family of a 16-year-old girl who was killed in a stabbing incident at a school in Bandar Utama last year, Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said today.
The
New Straits Times
reported that Kulasegaran said he would not comment further on the legal action as the matter involved the Ministry of Education and he did not have full details of the case.
“I don’t want to jump the gun. The actions by the government and the police will follow the normal process unless something unusual happens,” he told reporters after launching the Madani Kita Programme with the Buntong Community 2026 at the Kampung Tersusun Multipurpose Hall in Buntong here.
The civil suit was filed at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on October 1 by the mother and sister of Yap Shing Xuen, who was killed in the incident. According to a statement by Yap’s mother, the suit names several government agencies, the parents of the boy responsible for the fatal attack, and the boy himself as defendants.
The family said they believed the teenager’s death could have been prevented had appropriate measures been taken, particularly in addressing mental health issues among students.
Asked whether existing laws should be strengthened to include mental health provisions, Kulasegaran said the government was not currently drafting any new legislation on the matter. Instead, discussions were ongoing with relevant agencies and non-governmental organisations.
He also stressed the importance of helping parents better understand their children’s needs, including mental health concerns. Kulasegaran said he had recently met more than 1,000 parents during a programme in Serdang aimed at equipping them with skills to better support their children.
“The programme is conducted over 10 weeks, with three-hour sessions every weekend, to guide parents in understanding the needs of their children,” he said.
Kulasegaran noted that approaches to disciplining children had evolved over time, adding that mental health issues should be addressed more proactively. He said support should be extended to those affected, noting that mental health challenges also impacted a segment of the civil service.
“Action should be taken to help them,” he said.

Title: Rapid KL adds eight more shuttle buses as MRT Putrajaya Line repair work continues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Repair works are underway to restore power supply and train services on the Putrajaya Line following a cable theft near the Taman Equine MRT Station, according to Rapid KL.
It said alternative train services and free shuttle buses remained available to help passengers get to their destinations during the disruption.
“Alternative train services and free shuttle buses are still operating to assist passengers, with eight additional buses deployed to facilitate passenger movement,” it said in a statement.
The service disruption was caused by a loss of power following a cable theft near Taman Equine Station, which was detected at 5.24 am today.
Following the incident, a train was stranded at the station, while technical teams were mobilised to inspect the affected area and carry out the necessary repair works to restore power supply and train services.
Rapid KL also advised passengers travelling to Sepang via the ERL from Putrajaya Sentral to use alternative routes via the KL Sentral or Bandar Tasik Selatan ERL stations.
Station staff and auxiliary police personnel have also been deployed at stations and bus stops to help manage passenger movement.
Rapid KL said it would provide updates on the service status from time to time through its official social media channels. — Bernama

Title: Raincoat and umbrella check: Storm warning for KL, Putrajaya and six states until 4pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and six states until 4 pm today.
It said in a statement that the adverse weather was expected to affect Perak (Kuala Kangsar, Larut Matang, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Perak Tengah and Hilir Perak) and the whole of Selangor.
A similar warning was also issued for Kelantan (Pasir Puteh and Bachok) as well as Terengganu (Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus and Kuala Terengganu).
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Limbang (Limbang), Miri (Marudi), Sri Aman (Sri Aman and Lubok Antu), Betong (Betong), Bintulu (Tatau), Sibu (Selangau) and Kapit (Song).
As for Sabah, the areas involved are the Interior (Pensiangan, Sipitang, Tenom and Tambunan), Tawau (Kalabakan and Lahad Datu), Sandakan (Kinabatangan) and the West Coast. — Bernama

Title: Water in the tank at Batu Kawan? Penang team looks into viral claims of vehicle trouble after refuelling
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 4 — The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) in Penang is investigating claims that several vehicles experienced problems after refuelling at petrol stations near Batu Kawan.
A Penang KPDN spokesperson said the ministry was aware of the claims and had sent a team to investigate.
“The Penang KPDN has taken note of the claims of vehicles experiencing problems after refuelling at a petrol station near Batu Kawan.
“We will send a team to look into the matter and issue a media statement afterwards,” the spokesperson said in a statement today.
Earlier, several posts went viral on social media alleging that vehicles experienced problems, including being unable to start, after refuelling at several petrol stations around Penang.
The posts also claimed that the problem was suspected to have been caused by water-contaminated fuel, but this has yet to be confirmed by the authorities. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: The initials KPDN in Malay stands for Kementerian Perdagangan Dalam Negeri dan Kos Sara Hidup.
